_doc: Sector space (docs/CONTENT.md section 11; scripts/space/sector.gd makes a sector from a Drift node, radar.gd says what the ship sees of it). A sector is generated from the campaign seed and the node (same seed and node, same sector), never from the jump counter. size: the square region in px. arrival: the ship arrives `inset` px in from one edge (a seeded edge), `spread` of the edge's length either side of its middle. current: the debris current's speed range in px/s (its direction is any). pressure: the Hollow tide's pressure on a place (0 to 1, tide.gd pressure; the sector view creeps a fog in from the left as it grows) multiplies the debris density by lerp(1, `debris`, pressure), before the Hollow place's own multiplier. streams: the debris flows in `count` (min, max) streams, the main current and the rest side streams, each side stream rolled from the sector's seed with an angle `angle_off` (min, max degrees, to either side) off the main one, a speed in the current's range and a `share` (min, max) of the pieces; the main current carries the rest (data/debris.json streams). poi: `count` the least and most POIs of a sector, `dist` how far from the arrival point a POI sits, `gap` the least distance between two POIs (relaxed when a sector is crowded), `margin` how close to the edge a POI may sit, `trigger` the distance at which a new POI runs its event, `rearm` x trigger is how far a station or store must be left before it greets again, `spawn` how far from a POI a fight's enemy appears (min, max). far (no walls: the ship may fly on for ever, the square of `size` px only frames the placed layout, the arrival and the POIs above): past it space is cut into `chunk` px squares, and each chunk that does not touch that square rolls `count` (min, max) far POIs of its own, from an rng seeded by the sector seed mixed with the chunk's (x, y), so a chunk always gives the same ones; they are picked from the node's own `weights` times the multiplier of their type in `types` (only these types are ever far: no station, store, quest, exit beacon or checkpoint; a pirate nest is rare), sit at random inside the chunk, `poi.gap` from each other and from the placed POIs, and have the id f<x>_<y>_<i>. The chunks within `live` chunks of the ship's chunk are live (their POIs are in all_pois(): radar, triggers and the view see them); one the ship leaves drops out, and a far POI that is done stays done (saved). radar: `visual` the range at which anything (a hidden contact too) is seen with no radar, `helm` the range of the built-in Mk0 radar of a powered helm (no identification); other radar parts add stats.radar_range (px), stats.identify and stats.see_hidden (the Mk3: hidden contacts show within its range). ambient: every `every` seconds a roll with `chance` adds a passing ship (an `unknown` contact whose kind is picked by the region's `ambient` weights) at `edge` x the radar's range; it flies at `speed` px/s (min, max), comes to the ship with chance `approach` or passes by, leaves after `ttl` seconds, and at most `max` are about at once. poi_types: label, visibility (beacon: always on the radar; signal: needs a radar in range; hidden: seen only within the visual range; a weighted object is rolled), event (the event type its event is picked from, data/events; a weighted object is rolled; the main POI of a node always uses the node's own type), max (the most of this type in a sector), repeat (a station or store: it never becomes done, it greets once per visit and then only docks), dock (it opens the station menu when the node has one), flagship (a race flagship, data/flagships.json, scripts/space/flagships.gd: no node type weighs it, so it is never rolled; its `event` is a placeholder, its page is Flagships.event; Flagships.attach adds it to one sector of a homeland from its stage on, always a beacon; its page is Flagships.event, and it is done only when beaten), shop (it opens a small shop after its event, whatever the node: the stock is rolled per POI, data/drift.json shops), enemy (a ship design id that the POI's fights use instead of the tier roll; empty = the event decides), manual (the POI never triggers by itself: fly within `reach` px of it and press E to send an away team, scripts/space/expedition.gd and data/expeditions.json; its event type is exp_<kind>). nodes: per Drift node type, `main` the POI type that is always there (its event is the node's old arrival event), `also` POI types that are always there too (a pirate nest has a wreck, a store has a mining field), `count` the least and most POIs in all, `weights` POI type -> weight for the other POIs (0 or missing = never), `density` the debris density (x the base spawn rate and cap of data/debris.json) and `debris` debris type id -> weight multiplier (the theme). A `quest` weight counts only in a region that has a quest event of its own (sector.gd has_quest: the homeland tech quests of data/packs/regions_1), so there is no quest site where there is no quest. regions: the passing ships' `ambient` weights of a sector made without region data (a region file's own `ambient` is used in play, data/regions/*.json), by id; an unknown id uses the Boneyard's. The `exit` node is a region's exit beacon (docs/CONTENT.md section 15): its main POI is the `exit_beacon`, whose arrival opens the region choice. helm (scripts/space/helm.gd): out of combat the flight numbers (acceleration and top speed) run at `cruise` times, real again with a hostile within `real_within` px; the autopilot stops within `arrive` px of its course below `arrive_speed` px/s, plans its braking at `brake` times the reverse thrust, and steers round drifting debris of `avoid.size` px or more that lies within `avoid.look` px ahead (or `avoid.react` seconds at its speed) and closer to its line than its own radius plus the rock's and `avoid.clear`.

hollow._doc: In a Hollow place (the tide has taken it, sector.gd hollow) these replace the rolls above: a ghost (a `hollow` contact) every `every` seconds with `chance`, always closing in (`approach`), and the debris spawns at `debris` x its density. Ghosts count toward `max`.
